title: Video can start and end on your frames
summary:
Video gets start and end frames, transcripts get speaker labels, and 40 community additions give the app catalog a growth spurt.

Video requests now accept two positional images: the first sets the start frame and the second sets the end frame on veo, seedance, seedance-2.0, and wan-fast. A single image still works as before. Model listings now expose video capabilities, and the MCP video tool accepts durations up to 120 seconds for models that support them. Wan-fast's two-frame route produces a fixed five-second video without audio.

The transcription API added `response_format=diarized_json` for AssemblyAI and ElevenLabs Scribe. It returns speaker-labeled segments with text and timestamps, plus an optional `speakers_expected` hint when the speaker count is known.

The app catalog gained visual projects spanning comic panels, game assets, image editing, quote posters, and prompt-to-video. Among them, Film ze Snu turns dream descriptions or voice recordings into a four-scene film, while AI Clip Finder finds moments to clip from longer videos. These are community-made apps added to the catalog, not new Pollinations API features.

highlights.title: Set both video frames
highlights.text: Send a start image and an end image to supported video models, including `veo`, `seedance`, `seedance-2.0`, and `wan-fast`. One image still makes a normal image-to-video request. [Explore the API docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).

highlights.title: Speaker-labeled transcripts
highlights.text: Use `response_format=diarized_json` with AssemblyAI or ElevenLabs Scribe to get transcript segments labeled by speaker and timestamp. If you know how many speakers to expect, pass `speakers_expected`. [Explore the API docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).
